notes: The tutorial says 'Arduino MKR family board' without naming a model; the image looks like an MKR WiFi 1010 (the code comments mention MKR1000), so arduino-mkr-wifi-1010 is assumed. Any MKR board fits the same headers.
The MKR Motor Carrier is not in the catalogue, so it is a new part type. It has female header sockets for the MKR board and screw terminals for the battery (VIN/GND) and the motor outputs (M1-M4).

Fix for the validation errors: the carrier's screw-terminal ports are now kind 'header-socket' instead of 'lug'. The LiPo battery and DC motor expose 'lead' ports, and lead into a socket is a compatible join. The clamping action is still recorded as method=screw, reversible=tool.

The manual says the battery goes on the male pins or on the blue terminal block (VIN and GND). The terminal block is used here, with the lipo-battery bare leads screwed in. The catalogue lipo-battery has a JST connector.
The DC motor on M1+/M1- is optional but is included in the graph, as the circuit image shows.
Only the header pins the sketch relies on get port-specific edges: power (5V, VIN, VCC, GND) and the I2C and interrupt lines (11, 12, 6). The whole-board joined edge covers the remaining pins.
The carrier's on/off slide switch is flipped to ON. It is part of the carrier board, so it is not a separate node.
The micro USB cable plugs into the MKR board, with no host computer shown, so the cable has a joined edge with no ports named.
The optional bench power supply is an alternative to the LiPo battery and is not modelled.
